overallSummary: Fabio Giglietto maintains a strong, highly targeted professional social media presence across Mastodon, LinkedIn, and Bluesky, focusing heavily on computational social science, disinformation, and research tools. With a combined following of 3,580, his content consistently resonates with an academic and data-science-oriented audience, yielding solid engagement metrics particularly around research milestones and career opportunities.

contentThemes.description: Posts highlighting research, tools (like CooRnet), and conferences focused on detecting coordinated sharing and disinformation operations.
Announcements regarding research grants, paper publications, and speaking engagements.
Hiring posts for postdoc and PhD positions within computational social science.

recommendations: Leverage Bluesky's highly active sharing culture by posting more frequent, bite-sized research updates and thread-based summaries of new papers.
Capitalize on LinkedIn's high absolute engagement by adding direct links to application portals and interactive media for job openings to convert impressions into candidates.
Increase interaction on Mastodon by asking open-ended methodological questions to stimulate discussion within the academic instance audience.

platformInsights.bluesky: Bluesky shows the highest engagement rate (average 6.14%), driven largely by strong community reposting behavior, making it excellent for amplifying research papers and student opportunities.
platformInsights.mastodon: Mastodon provides stable engagement (average 4.55%) on specialized updates such as tool releases (CooRnet v2.0), but benefits from more technical, development-focused discussions.
platformInsights.linkedin: LinkedIn has the largest follower base (1,850) and generates the highest absolute engagement, making it the premier platform for high-impact announcements like grants and job openings.

topPerformingContent.content: Just published our new paper on coordinated inauthentic behavior on social media platforms!
New research opportunity for PhD students interested in computational social science. Reply for details!
Excited to announce that our research team has been awarded a new grant to study information operations across social media platforms.
